Developing Experts × Clean Energy Technical Excellence College · East of England

Try the jobs that will power the East, and power the country

Offshore wind, nuclear, solar, domestic renewables and the grid are creating thousands of skilled jobs along the Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex coast. Virtual work experience (VWE) lets every learner try them, wherever they live: twelve VWEs, six to build it and six to run it, each leading to a real apprenticeship, T Level or degree route at a CETEC college.

The regional strategy

Inspire, engage, recruit: one plan for the region’s clean energy workforce

This platform is the proposed recruitment, inspiration and engagement strategy for the Clean Energy Technical Excellence College (CETEC). It is led by Colchester Institute with Suffolk New College, East Coast College and City College Norwich as core delivery partners, working with Sizewell C, EDF, Freeport East, EEEGR and EastWind. It joins schools, colleges and employers in one learner journey, from a first spark of interest to a job offer.

1

Inspire

Every young person sees clean energy as their future

  • Developing Experts lessons from KS2 to KS5 link science, maths and geography to local energy jobs
  • 30-minute career tasters and the one-day VWE reach every school in the region
  • Role tasters, the career finder and films for families and parents
  • Targeted reach into coastal, rural and former industrial towns, where placements are hardest to find
Measure: schools and learners reached, by postcode and group
2

Engage

Learners try the work, with employers, before they choose

  • Twelve five-day VWEs co-designed with industry partners, six to build it and six to run it
  • Mapped to apprenticeships and T Levels at the four CETEC colleges
  • Gatsby Benchmarks 4, 5 and 6 evidence for every school
  • Inclusive by design: BSL, read aloud, translation and SEND adaptations
Measure: VWE completions, interest before and after, course applications
3

Recruit

Evidence, not CVs, opens the door to a job

  • Every VWE produces an evidence report that replaces the CV
  • Learners apply with it; applicants are rank-ordered on what they did
  • Every applicant hears back: no more silence
  • Jobs board, talent pipeline and NEET outcomes shared with partners
Measure: applications, apprenticeship and job starts, NEET outcomes
CETEC collegesCourses, T Levels and apprenticeships; host VWEs in class and in adult learning; link learners to employers.
Industry partnersCo-design VWE scenarios and films; spotlight jobs; review evidence reports; post vacancies.
SchoolsRun tasters and VWEs in lessons; record Gatsby evidence; support families.
Developing ExpertsBuild and host the VWEs, lessons, AI tools, microcredentials, jobs board and data dashboards.
Proposed phasing

Pilot 2027, then scale

Pilot six VWEs that cover all five focus areas: 1 offshore wind installation, 3 electrical and grid connection, 4 nuclear new build, 7 wind turbine technician, 8 nuclear operations and 10 data, drones and digital twins. Add the other six in phase 2. Employer partners for each VWE are proposed and to be agreed.

Access to work experience · the Developing Experts solution

Real work experience for every learner, anywhere

Work experience still depends on postcode and connections. Placements cluster near big employers, leaving coastal, rural and former industrial towns behind: exactly the places along this coast where the clean energy jobs are being created.

50%of Free School Meals pupils get work experience, against 61% of their peers
89applications per school-leaver vacancy at large UK employers
81%of job seekers have applied and heard nothing back in the past year
91%of under-24s want a human, not an algorithm, to review their application

One connected platform

Curriculum-linked VWEKS4 and KS5 virtual work experience, plus KS3 career lessons and a teacher training film.
AI learning toolsA suite of AI tools. Developing Experts is a DfE AI Tutoring Pioneer, with PA Consulting.
MicrocredentialsStackable, employer-validated credentials that carry learners from school into work.
Workforce dataReach, aspirations and skills gaps tracked over time, for colleges and employers.
Careers library and jobs board1,000+ roles across 30+ job families, easy to navigate.
Accessibility and inclusionAdaptations so every learner can take part, wherever they live.

Build it, then run it

Every energy project needs two workforces

Build teams survey, design, make and install wind farms, power stations, substations and solar. Operations teams run and maintain them for 25 to 60 years. Some careers bridge both, and those are some of the most in-demand jobs of all.

Build

Build and install

Engineers, welders, steel fixers, electricians, cable jointers, crane operators, project managers and the scientists who win permission to build.

See build careers →
Both

Bridge the two

Commissioning engineers, asset integrity and reliability engineers, rope access technicians and safety leaders turn a new build into a working plant.

See bridge careers →
Operate

Operate and maintain

Wind turbine and nuclear technicians, grid control engineers, vessel crews, solar and heat pump installers, data analysts and more, many with paid apprenticeships.

See operate careers →

Jargon buster

What the words mean

Plain-English meanings for the terms used on this site.

CETEC
Clean Energy Technical Excellence College. In the East it is led by Colchester Institute with Suffolk New College, East Coast College and City College Norwich.
VWE (virtual work experience)
Online work experience. You watch films, answer quizzes and make decisions in simulations set by real employers, and earn a certificate.
Apprenticeship
A paid job with training. You earn a wage, study part of the week and gain a qualification, with no tuition fees.
Foundation apprenticeship
A level 2 apprenticeship for young people that gives a broad start in a sector, such as engineering or construction.
Apprenticeship levels
Level 2 is like GCSEs, level 3 like A levels, levels 4 and 5 like the first years of a degree, level 6 a degree and level 7 a master’s degree.
Degree apprenticeship
A level 6 or 7 apprenticeship where you earn a full degree while working, with no student debt.
T Level
A two-year course after GCSEs, equal to three A levels, with a 45-day industry placement. Examples: Engineering, Manufacturing, Processing and Control, and Building Services Engineering.
Evidence report
The report you get after a VWE. It shows what you did and the skills you showed, and you can use it when you apply.
Gatsby Benchmarks
Eight national standards for good careers education in schools and colleges. VWEs help schools meet them.
Offshore wind
Wind turbines built out at sea, where winds are stronger. The East of England has more installed offshore wind than any other UK region.
O&M (operations and maintenance)
Running and looking after an energy site once it is built, often for 25 years or more.
GWO training
Global Wind Organisation basic safety training: the courses you need before working on wind turbines.
Grid
The network of cables, pylons and substations that moves electricity from where it is made to where it is used.
Substation
A site that changes the voltage of electricity so it can travel long distances or be used in homes.
Nuclear new build
Building a new nuclear power station, such as Sizewell C on the Suffolk coast.
Green hydrogen
Hydrogen gas made by splitting water with clean electricity. It can fuel lorries, ships and industry.
Domestic renewables
Clean energy at home: solar panels, heat pumps, batteries and insulation.
Freeport
An area with special tax and customs rules to encourage investment, such as Freeport East at Felixstowe and Harwich.
CSCS card
The card most building sites ask to see, showing you have passed a health and safety test.
NEET
Not in education, employment or training. Usually used about 16 to 24 year olds.
Commissioning
Testing every system in a new plant before it is switched on.
Social value
The extra good a big project does for local people, such as jobs, training and work with schools.

Questions people ask

What is virtual work experience?

Online work experience where you try a real job through films, quizzes and simulations designed with employers. Each of the 12 VWEs runs as a five-day, 25-hour placement for KS4 and KS5, or a 30-minute career taster that spotlights one career. You earn a certificate and an evidence report you can use to apply. See the VWEs.

What is CETEC?

The Clean Energy Technical Excellence College for the East. It is led by Colchester Institute, with Suffolk New College, East Coast College and City College Norwich as core delivery partners, and works with industry partners including Sizewell C, EDF, Freeport East, EEEGR and EastWind. Its focus is offshore wind, nuclear, solar, domestic renewables and grid infrastructure.

Why the East of England?

The East coast hosts a large share of the UK’s offshore wind, a new nuclear power station at Sizewell C, the UK’s biggest container port at Felixstowe and growing solar, storage and grid projects. These all need skilled people, many of them locally.

When will the jobs start?

Many are open now, especially in offshore wind operations, electrical work and nuclear construction. More will follow as new wind farms, Sizewell C and grid upgrades move through build into decades of operation.

Do I need to work offshore?

No. Many clean energy jobs are onshore: in ports, factories, control rooms, offices, labs, substations and people’s homes. Offshore roles need safety training such as GWO and a medical, which employers often help with.

Do I need a degree?

No. Many roles start with an apprenticeship, a T Level or on-the-job training, including wind turbine technician, electrician, welder, port operative and solar installer. Engineering can also be reached by a degree apprenticeship, so you earn while you learn.

I'm an adult changing career. Is it too late?

No. Apprenticeships have no upper age limit, and skills from trades, driving, the forces, fishing, and oil and gas count. Ask a CETEC college about adult courses and Skills Bootcamps, and see the crossover routes.

    From lesson to VWE

    Every VWE is hosted here and on Developing Experts, and signposted from lessons

    When a pupil learns about cells in biology, circuits in physics or area in maths, the Developing Experts lesson shows them the clean energy careers that use it and links straight to the matching VWE. Learners can do the VWE on this microsite or on Developing Experts: it is the same VWE, and their progress and evidence report count in both places.

    1. LessonA Developing Experts lesson, e.g. cells in Year 8 biology
    2. Signpost"Who uses this?" card shows clean energy careers
    3. VWEThe learner starts the VWE here or on Developing Experts
    4. EvidenceEvidence report and badges are saved
    5. Next stepsBack here for pathways, partners and jobs
    Why this helps schools engage
    • Fits lessons teachers already teach: the VWE link sits inside a Developing Experts lesson, so there is no extra planning.
    • Gatsby Benchmark 4 in every subject: linking curriculum learning to careers, with Benchmarks 5 and 6 evidence when pupils do the VWE.
    • Works where pupils are: start in class on Developing Experts, or at home on this microsite. Progress and the evidence report count in both places.
    • Local and real: pupils see the clean energy jobs on their own coastline, with the employers that will hire.

    Building traffic to Developing Experts. Every link to a VWE on Developing Experts carries campaign tags (source, VWE, hub), so lesson and microsite visits can be counted in the impact dashboards.

    Policy watch · November 2026

    Apprenticeship and T Level changes built into the mapping

    Foundation apprenticeships

    Level 2, for 16 to 21 year olds (up to 24 with an EHC plan, for care leavers, or for people in or leaving prison). Used as the first rung in VWEs 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 11, subject to which sectors offer them.

    Find an apprenticeship ↗
    Onsite Construction T Level closed

    No new enrolments after the September 2024 cohort. Trade routes now run through apprenticeships, with Design, Surveying and Planning for technical roles.

    T Levels update ↗
    Level 7 for younger learners

    Since January 2026, level 7 apprenticeships are limited to younger learners. Marked * in each pathway; check eligibility with the provider.

    FE Week ↗
    Management standards changes, September 2026

    Some management standards, including Team Leader (L3) and Operations Manager (L5), changed from September 2026. Not mapped; check current status on Skills England.

    Skills England ↗

    Mapping to be validated against Skills England occupational standards and with the CETEC colleges before launch. Check entry requirements with the training provider.

The yearly income uses a 4% draw-down rule of thumb. Many energy employers pay well above 3%; ask at interview. You get tax relief on what you pay in.

      Money words explained

      Gross pay

      Your pay before anything is taken off.

      Take-home (net) pay

      What reaches your bank account after tax, National Insurance, pension and any student loan.

      Personal allowance

      The first £12,570 you earn each year is tax-free.

      Income tax

      20% on earnings from £12,570 to £50,270 (basic rate), 40% above (higher rate). Your tax code tells your employer how much allowance you get, usually 1257L.

      National Insurance

      8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270, then 2%. It counts towards your State Pension.

      Pension

      Money saved for later life. In the NHS Pension Scheme you pay 5.2% to 12.5% and your employer adds 23.7%. Other employers must add at least 3%.

      Student loan

      You only repay once you earn over the threshold: 9% of earnings above £29,385 (Plan 2) or £25,000 (Plan 5). It stops when you earn less, and is written off after 30 or 40 years.

      Shift and offshore allowances

      Extra pay some energy jobs add for nights, rotas or working offshore. It varies by employer.

      Unsocial hours

      Extra NHS pay for evenings, nights, weekends and bank holidays, as a percentage of your hourly rate.

      Overtime

      Hours worked above your normal week. In construction it is often paid at time and a half.

      Council tax

      A local tax on your home, paid monthly to the council. If you live alone you get 25% off.

      Lifetime ISA

      A savings account for a first home for people aged 18 to 39. The government adds 25% to up to £4,000 a year.

        In-demand roles

        Which jobs does the region need most?

        Each role gets a demand score out of 100 from five signals: live vacancies, what the region’s energy projects need, workforce gaps, retirements and how few people are training for it. Use it to choose a VWE with strong job prospects, or to plan training and recruitment.

        Illustrative scores. Live vacancies come from the jobs board; the other signals are example values. The live system takes them from the data sources listed below.

        All roles, ranked

        How the score works, and adjust it

        Each signal is scored 0 to 100, then combined using the weights below. Move a slider to change how much a signal counts. Critical is 72 or more, High 63 to 71, Rising 54 to 62, and anything lower is Steady.

        Data sources for the live system

        • Live vacancies: the partner feeds on this site (Find an apprenticeship, cluster member feeds, partner careers sites), plus regional job-postings data
        • Programme need: employers' labour plans for Sizewell C, offshore wind, grid and port projects, by trade and year
        • Workforce gap: EastWind workforce research, CITB Construction Skills Network forecasts and nuclear sector workforce data for the East of England
        • Retirement risk: workforce age profiles from employers; industry age data
        • Pipeline: VWE completions on this site, plus CETEC college, apprenticeship and university starts
        • Local priorities: the Local Skills Improvement Plans for Norfolk and Suffolk, and Essex, Southend and Thurrock
